items.why: An Enclosure design product was added to the navigation with no price change.
The Pro button copy changed from Get started for free to Try for $0.00 with no price change.
A feature row was renamed from Coding sessions to Cloud coding agent, still Included.
A note that additional Classroom seats can be purchased was added, with no price shown or changed.
The Sandboxes beta runtime cap of up to 30 days on Pro and above was replaced with Can run indefinitely.

record.short: Render Sandboxes runtime goes from up to 30 days on Pro and above to Can run indefinitely.
record.headline: Render removed the 30-day runtime limit on Sandboxes, its beta isolated environments for agents, and now says they can run indefinitely.
record.who: Users of the Sandboxes beta on Pro and above.
record.read: Render is promoting Sandboxes for agent workloads with a new banner, and lifting the runtime cap fits that push. Billing stays usage-based on CPU, so longer runs mean more spend rather than a price change.
record.caveat: The compute table on the same page still lists a 24 hours maximum session length for some plans, so the page is not fully consistent. The product is in beta.

items.why: Two new models (Kimi K3.1 Pro, Ripple-65B Preview) were added to the price list with no change to existing prices.
The Pro plan Notetaker history changed from Longer to Unlimited.

record.short: Flow Pro Notetaker history goes from Longer Notetaker history to Unlimited Notetaker history.
record.headline: Wispr Flow now lists Notetaker history as unlimited on its paid plan, where it previously said longer.
record.who: Paying Flow Pro subscribers; the wording appears in both plan listings on the page.
record.read: Following last week’s move to unlimited meetings on Pro, this is another loosening of Notetaker limits, which looks like a push to make the paid tier more attractive against Free.
record.caveat: The earlier wording gave no number, so the size of the increase is unknown.

items.why: A webinar banner was added at the top of the page.
The Team plan entry point moved from $29.99 for 3,000 credits back to $49.99 for 5,000 credits, reversing last week’s change.

record.short: Team plan entry point moves from $29.99/mo for 3,000 credits to $49.99/mo for 5,000 credits, and the 3,000 and 4,000 credit steps are removed.

items.why: The text billed annually was dropped after the $199/mo. price while the 12 months commitment and price stayed the same.
Spelling changed from British to American English and a stray character was fixed.
Only a customer-count claim line was removed; no pricing content changed in either captured version.
An expired event banner was removed.
The Basic plan now lists 25 credits / month included for advanced AI features.

record.short: Basic plan now lists 25 credits / month included for AI Pentesting, Deep PR Reviews and AI Code Analysis.

items.why: Three prices each moved by $1 ($96 → $95, $161 → $160, $561 → $560), which looks like currency rounding rather than a decided change.
The compliance list was reordered and ISO 27701 was dropped from the list, with no price or plan change.
Only the G2 review count changed.
A limited-time offer was added that makes Browser Use runs free, which previously charged max_cost_usd per accepted task.

promo.text: Limited-time offer: Browser Use runs are free (max_cost_usd is required)

items.why: The header call to action changed from Switch to Anrok to Book a demo.
The overage copy now says the widget stops working only if overage is turned off; the $25 per 5,000 MAU price is unchanged.
A duplicated mobile menu call to action was removed.
